answer.question: How does a pond affect a small Nocatee turf layout?
answer.answer: Where Florida’s residential standard applies, turf generally needs a 10-foot separation from the pond’s high-water line, with an exception for a separating seawall or bulkhead. Swales and pond littoral areas stay clear. Establish that boundary and any maintenance access before deciding how much yard can be turfed.

blocks.kicker: Between the lanai and the boundary
blocks.h2: Choose the most useful area first.
paras: A pet area close to the door, a lawn for everyday use and a compact green each need different space. On a narrow lot, compare one primary use before trying to fit all three. For putting, leave standing room and a clear route around the surface.
Many newer yards have limited shade. Think about when the area will be used and how people or pets can get out of full sun; turf can become hot.

blocks.h2: Confirm who controls each part of the plan.
paras: Nocatee has different neighborhood associations and CDDs, and spans St. Johns and Duval counties. Use the exact property and community when requesting the applicable requirements. An architectural committee’s response and CDD conditions should be checked for the actual work area.

Mark pond edges, swales, easements and preserve boundaries on the plan. A rear fence does not establish permission to use every strip within it. Bring the written conditions to the estimate, together with existing irrigation and drainage information.

blocks.h2: A back yard a few strides deep has to work hard.
paras: Nocatee's builders sell lots by their width: 40-foot lots in Daniel Park at Town Center, 40-, 50- and 60-foot lots at The Crossing at Twenty Mile, 60- and 70-foot lots at The Outlook (Nocatee). On the narrower lots, the back yard between the lanai and the rear line is a few strides deep, and on a large share of them that line is a retention pond or the edge of a preserve.

Grass can't recover in a space that small. Two kids and a dog cross the same few feet all day, and the builder's sod gives out along the fence first. If yours has already been replaced once, turf ends the cycle: no bare path, no mud at the slider, nothing to reseed.
Most lots here get full sun, because the trees are young. Lots that back onto the preserve in Crosswater and Coastal Oaks have more mature canopy, and more shade.

blocks.h2: Your architectural committee approves the yard; the CDD runs the parks.
paras: Nocatee runs on two layers. The Tolomato Community Development District, in the St. Johns County part, and the Split Pine CDD, in the Duval part, own and run the common ground: Splash Water Park, the Nocatee Swim Club, Greenleaf Pavilion and the parks (Tolomato CDD). Your neighborhood's HOA and its architectural committee govern your yard. Approval goes neighborhood by neighborhood, so ask yours for its turf standard in writing.

Behind a privacy fence, Florida law is your strongest card. An HOA can't restrict turf that isn't visible from the frontage, a neighboring lot, a common area or a community golf course (Fla. Stat. 720.3045). A fenced interior lot usually clears that test; a yard open to a pond or a common area may not.

One recent change matters here more than almost anywhere. Since 1 July 2026, the state's protection from local turf bans doesn't reach a community development district enforcing deed restrictions (SB 1180). Before the layout is settled, ask your CDD in writing whether it enforces any that touch turf; our guide to Florida HOAs and turf explains the change.

blocks.h2: JEA's purple pipe, and the days it ran dry.
paras: Nocatee's lawns water from JEA's reclaimed system, the purple pipe, and it has struggled to hold pressure. From 7 April 2025, JEA split Nocatee into four watering zones, set days by zone instead of by address, and made reclaimed water unavailable two days a week (JEA). That schedule ran until 2 November 2025, when the standard rules came back (JEA Nocatee watering).

Across St. Johns County, a Phase III water shortage order has limited utility and well irrigation to one day a week since 11 May 2026, and new sod is restricted (St. Johns County). Reclaimed water is exempt from that cap, but it has limits of its own here. Turf takes the lawn off both schedules.

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in Nocatee, FL?
faq.a: We install artificial turf, pet turf and backyard putting greens in Nocatee, FL. Many Nocatee homes sit on 40- or 50-foot lots whose small back yards often end at a pond or a preserve, and Florida's turf standard keeps turf 10 feet from a pond's water line. Your neighborhood's architectural committee signs off on the plan. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

Palm Valley Golf Club, a 9-hole executive course open since 1989, sits in the middle of Nocatee and has a 10,000 square foot practice putting green (GolfPass). The championship courses, TPC Sawgrass among them, are a short drive east across the Intracoastal. At home, a green with two cups and a fringe fits most Nocatee yards.

By mailing address, usually. Ponte Vedra 32081 is the inland ZIP code west of the Intracoastal, and most of it is Nocatee; Ponte Vedra Beach, 32082, is the ocean side across the water. The ground, the lots and the rules are different on each side.

faq.q: What will my architectural committee want to see?
faq.a: Usually a plot plan, the turf's spec sheet, details of the base and infill, and a physical sample. Committees also weigh drainage, how real the turf looks and how it fits the street. The layout you approve with us before work starts gives you the plot plan.

faq.q: Will turf get too hot for the dog?
faq.a: In full summer sun it can, the way a patio can, and most Nocatee yards are in full sun. Put the dog's corner where it gets afternoon shade and keep a water bowl there (how hot turf gets). Pet turf drains when the dog goes and rinses clean with a hose.
